## Core processing architecture

::: {.kicker}
Pipeline architecture
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.flow-row}
::: {.node .pale-indigo}
**Planning + L0 inbox**
<br><br>
Science timelines and FITS
:::
::: {.arrow}
->
:::
::: {.node .pale-blue}
**Intake + validation**
<br><br>
Register timeline plans, then validate L0
:::
::: {.arrow}
->
:::
::: {.node .pale-cyan}
**PostgreSQL state**
<br><br>
Claims, Retries, Products, Lineage
:::
::: {.arrow}
->
:::
::: {.node .pale-green}
**L1 workers**
<br><br>
Per-exposure processing
:::
::: {.arrow}
->
:::
::: {.node .pale-green}
**L2 processing**
<br><br>
Delivery of L0 closed (+12 hours after observation); All L1 processed successfully
:::
::: {.arrow}
->
:::
::: {.node .pale-blue}
**Published products**
<br><br>
Current L1/L2 outputs
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
Dagster is for operator control with launcher and maintenance schedules.
It is does not act as the authoritative source for the processing
:::

## Authority boundaries

::: {.kicker}
Pipeline architecture
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.grid-3}
::: {.card .pale-blue}
::: {.label .blue}
Git
:::

- Source code for the pipeline
- Source code for the science
- Source code for the FITS keywords
- Will contain all science and deployment configuration
- Tests, CI, documentation, changelog and release
:::

::: {.card .pale-green}
::: {.label .green}
PostgreSQL
:::

- Workflow state
- Claims, Leases, Retries
- Observations and Product bookkeeping
:::

::: {.card .pale-cyan}
::: {.label .cyan}
Filesystem
:::

- Planning publications and L0 files
- Staged and Published science products
- Outputs are stored outside of the containers
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
The pipeline is fully containerized
:::

## Design Assumptions

::: {.kicker}
Pipeline architecture
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .pale-green}
::: {.label .green}
Assumptions currently made
:::

- Planning is published before its L0 files arrive=
- Observation windows never overlap
- L0 files arrive and are all accounted for, there are none lost in transit
  - Pipeline checks the hashes are correct
  - I assume the keywords in the FITs header will be able to tell us how many files we can expect?
- L0 files are un-writeable by the pipeline
- L0 files are N parallel, they don't need any information from other L0 files
- L0 files can be processed as soon as they arrive, we don't need to wait for anything
- Everything is "simple" - One database, individual workers, one orchestrator, html dashboard for database status
  - This all split up, so can be deployed onto different machines (with some work)
:::

::: {.card .pale-red}
::: {.label .red}
Complexity to avoid without requirements
:::

- Complex dispatch systems like kubernetes
  - Useful if we want to scale up or use multiple worker machines
- Using the filesystem to scan and manage the state of the pipeline or file processing
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
Are they correct?
:::
